name: Mirchi ka Salan
subtitle: long green chillies in a thick peanut, sesame and tamarind gravy

ingredients.qty: 10 large mild bhavnagri, slit lengthways, seeds scraped out
ingredients.note: the fat pale ones, not the thin hot ones
any more turns the gravy bitter
salan is meant to be an oily gravy

prepNotes: Soak the tamarind in hot water for 20 minutes and squeeze out a thick pulp; strain and keep the liquid.
Slit the chillies down one side and scrape out the seeds and ribs with a teaspoon handle — that is where nearly all the heat sits.
Dry-roast the peanuts, sesame and coconut ahead and let them cool fully before grinding, or the paste turns oily and grainy.

steps.text: Dry-roast the peanuts in a kadhai over medium heat for 5 minutes until the skins blister and loosen, then rub off the skins in a cloth.
Roast the sesame in the same pan for 1 minute until it pops, then the dried coconut for 1 minute until it smells nutty and turns pale gold. Cool completely.
Grind the peanuts, sesame and coconut with 150ml water to a fine, smooth paste. Set aside.
steps.tip: Grind for longer than you think — any grit here stays gritty in the finished dish.

steps.text: Heat 3 tbsp of the oil and fry the slit chillies for 2-3 minutes, turning, until the skins blister and go khaki. Lift them out and reserve.
In the same oil, fry the chopped onion until soft and light brown, about 8 minutes, then cool and grind to a paste.
Add the rest of the oil to the pan and crackle the cumin, mustard, fenugreek and nigella, then throw in the curry leaves.
steps.tip: The fenugreek should barely change colour — dark fenugreek is bitter.

steps.text: Add the ginger and garlic pastes and fry 1 minute until the raw smell goes, then the onion paste, turmeric, chilli powder and coriander powder. Cook 3 minutes.
Stir in the ground peanut-sesame paste and fry on medium-low for 8-10 minutes, stirring often, until the mixture darkens and oil rises around the edges.
steps.tip: This is the step that decides the dish. Undercooked paste tastes raw and chalky.

steps.text: Pour in the tamarind water and the remaining water, add salt and the jaggery, and simmer uncovered 12 minutes until glossy and the thickness of pouring cream.
Slide the fried chillies back in, cover and simmer 5 minutes more, then rest off the heat 10 minutes and scatter with coriander leaves.
steps.tip: The chillies should stay whole — stir gently or not at all once they are back in.

storage: Keeps 4 days refrigerated and tastes better on day two. The oil sets on top when cold; warm it gently on the stove and stir it back in, adding a splash of water if it has tightened.
